item.content:encoded: This is still the gold standard for launching a new group of interest and given the avalanche of groups that have followed in its wake, probably one of the most influential pieces of fiction ever penned in this community. You could make a solid case for it being the most influential, given that it represents a watershed moment in how Groups of Interest evolved from a static rogues gallery to an expansive and interconnected representation of the world behind the veil.

item.title: The true origin of AWCY?
item.content:encoded:
It’s interesting seeing the real first author of a thing’s interpretation of that thing. This reminds me of 1981, what with the crazed speech and lacerations. Notably, there’s a lot less emphasis on the art itself and more about the group, the brand “Are we cool yet?” I feel like it’s something that AWCY? sort of moves away from, giving way to more personal stories.

This is a great history lesson, though.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The Serpent's Hand only superfluously resembles the Chaos Insurgency. They represent a different worldview from the Foundation - one that sees the world as inherently complex and mystical, the mirror image to the Foundation's desire to preserve a certain flavor of normalcy. Two different views on How Things Should Be.

I agree the Factory & Wondertainment are similar in profile, but they produce SCPs that are very distinct from each other. The Factory mass produces things and almost (but not always) has an undertone of malice. Wondertainment makes 'limited runs' or collector's items, and there really isn't much malice involved (harm, sure, but not malice).

The University is an … Uh, pretty damn specific flavor of otherworldy weirdness.

The GOC is mentioned in a lot of tales, as I recall (particularly since Clef's backstory involves coming from the GOC).

"Nobody" is a really interesting piece of Foundation pseudo-canon. Just because it/he is underused doesn't mean it/he doesn't have potential. (In fact, like Mr. Freeze in the 1900s Batman animated series - semi-obscure reference! - he's better for being underused.)

The IRG is pretty… Eh, admittedly. And the UIU is a silly X-Files thing without much point but it's not hurting anything. Same for Prometheus Labs, and "Eric" for that matter.

I don't see "do we need it" as a really relevant question. I mean, we don't really need a wiki at all, but it sure is a lot of fun.

Better to ask 'is it causing any problems?' In this case, no, "Are We Cool Yet?" isn't. It also has four decently-to-well-rated SCPs plus this Tale under its belt. You could say this GOI is helping because it's inspiring people to create SCPs related to it, and it's hard to see why that might be a bad thing.

item.content:encoded:
Hmm, I normally agree with your comments, but here I sort of think you shot a billygoat.

Firstly, this isn't an effort by a single author - for example, the only one who really wrote stuff for the IRG was Bijhan, and he's been gone for some time, then reappeared briefly, then gone again.
Same goes with some potential redundancy -given there's little official canon on the site, anyone with their arse split in two can go out and make a group of interest and it's perfectly allright.

Second, and this is to go with a storytelling perspective, I actually like that there's redundancy because it makes it more realistic. In the real world you don't have a single group for every purpose, you have an ugly mess of coinciding interests and subtle or not-so-subtle differences wherever human effort is involved. Just as an example, take political parties, churches, linux distributions…..
Forcing to have just one for each type of action makes it look like power rangers instead - no matter what's the monster of the week, Rita Repulsa and Lord Zed are the ones behind it you can bet.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Gah. Another GOI. There's so many of them, you can't help but suspect every kindergarten is really an undercover group dealing with paranormal activities.

Let me take a look at the ones we currently have:

  • Alexylva University - alive and well-represented.
  • Army of the Guardians of the Islamic Revolution - briefly mentioned in the now-dead sex hating sphere and White Div skull. No activity.
  • The Chaos Insurgency - mentioned in a couple of tales.
  • The Church of the Broken God - more or less stable.
  • Doctor Wondertainment - more or less stable.
  • "Eric" - several random toys are enough to call something a group of interest.
  • The Factory - represented quite well.
  • The Global Occult Coalition (GOC) - mostly mentioned as a GOI, there's little activity otherwise.
  • Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd. - well-represented with their "capitalist sharks meet paranormal" profile.
  • "Nobody" - I only remember one tale.
  • Prometheus Labs, Inc. - mentioned for Telekill sake. No other activities.
  • The Serpent's Hand - mentioned in several objects/tales. Still kicking, outlook not so good.
  • Unusual Incidents Unit (UIU), Federal Bureau of Investigation - mentioned in Scantron's proposal and in some other tale. No activity.

So about half of these groups have no activity.

The Chaos Insurgency and The Serpent's Hand share the same profile - raiding Sites, devious plans and hidden meanings.
The Factory and Doctor Wondertainment share the same profile - manufacturing weird crap for profit and not getting caught. MC&D border on that too, but they don't mass-produce.

All in all, there are five groups of actual interest. Alexylva for otherworldly weirdness, Chaos Insurgency for messing with the Foundation, CotBG for religious fanatism, Factory for mass-producing weird stuff and MC&D for serious paranormal business. 8 other groups are either dead or redundant.

And you are creating another one.

Do we need it?

A few of the others say hi. Remember Miley from the thing in Alaska? She's made a full recovery and will be helping out at our next… exhibition.

This line crammed the memory of SCP-804 into my head so hard my eyes watered as they tried to pop out of the sockets.

And the OSSIFY WALL STREET signs, intended to blend in with the OCCUPY WALL STREET signs, ether as part of a ritual, or as a subliminal message for the viewers, that says that this group is thinking several steps ahead, planting the seeds of future activities in the current ones.

Serious upvote.
